newsitem.title: USA: Cold, ice seize much of United States.
newsitem.headline: Cold, ice seize much of United States.

text.p: Bitter cold seized much of the eastern two-thirds of the United States Friday, sending winter chills as far south as Florida.
The Pacific Northwest was hit with a new round of cold rain, with ice and heavy snow in mountain regions.

Forecasters had some good news -- temperatures in the 20's F (11's Celsius) in the upper Midwest beginning this weekend -- a warmup that would open the way for cleanup efforts in parts of the Dakotas and Minnesota struggling with house-high snowdrifts after a parade of blizzards.

It was minus nine degrees F (-23 Celsius) in Chicago at daybreak. Most schools were closed for the second day in row, not so much by the absolute cold as by winds that could quickly freeze exposed skin.
Lows fell into the teens (-10.5 to -7.7 C) in the Florida Panhandle.
In Miami, where Friday's high temperature was expected to remain below 60 F (16 C), tourists shivered at seaside cafes and stayed out of the chilly surf.
The city's bicycle-riding police officers wore their usual uniform of shorts and crew socks, but several also pulled on jackets because of the unseasonably cold temperatures.
In South Dakota officials ordered snowplows to work around the clock. On Thursday a plough operating near Pukwana found a stranded car with two men inside frozen to death and a third in bad shape.
South Dakota officials were also trying to round up some buffalo that fled their confines at a ranch when snow topped fences. About 300 of the animals were still at large.
In North Dakota one report estimated that 20,000 head of cattle were facing death.

Schools reopened Friday in Minnesota but officials worried about what would happen this spring when all the snow melts. Gov. Arne Carlson said he was worried about the potential for major spring flooding, and proposed a $20 million fund to help municipalities pay for snow removal.
In upstate New York the village of Montague celebrated a new U.S. record for the most snowfall in a single day, nearly 78 inches (196 cm) that fell during a storm last week.

Just 64 people live in the town, which is the country's leading producer of Philadelphia brand cream cheese. The residents decided to commemmorate the record by sending a case of cream cheese packed in snow to the people of Silver Lake, Colorado, the town that previously held the record.
Silver Lake recorded 76 inches (193 cm) in April 1921.
